title: Don't Worry Boys

description.main: A survey of Stanley Stellar's first two decades photographing gay New York, edited from his archive by Jordan Hancock, with a text by Andrew Holleran.
description.extended:
A survey of Stanley Stellar's first two decades photographing gay New York, from the West Village streets and piers of the late 1970s to studio portraits made during the AIDS crisis, edited from his archive by Jordan Hancock.

Stellar, a Brooklyn native, picked up a camera in 1976 and turned it on his own community: Christopher Street, the West Village, and the abandoned West Side piers that served for a few years as sunbathing ground, cruising ground and stage. He contributed to the literary magazine Christopher Street, the newspaper New York Native and the gay skin magazines of the period. The book keeps that range and sets frank daylight sex beside unguarded portraits. The later studio portraits were made as the epidemic took hold. Of the hundreds of men who sat for him then, only a handful are still alive. The title is taken from a New York social club. The book has 45 colour and 55 duotone plates, a text by the novelist Andrew Holleran, and design by LJ Studio.

Stellar (b. 1945) lives and works in Manhattan and has photographed the city's gay life for five decades, including the first Pride marches. Earlier books include The Beauty of All Men: Photographs 1976–2011 (All Saints Press) and The Piers (Kapp Kapp, 2023).
